title: What If Apollo's Footprints Stay on the Moon for Millions of Years?

scenes.text: What if your footprint outlived every building on Earth? On the Moon, it can.
The Moon has no wind and no rain, so nothing blows the dust around or washes it away.
Only micrometeorites wear tracks down, striking at over 33,000 miles an hour.
Even so, Apollo moon rocks show erosion of only about 0.04 inches per million years.
A lunar scientist estimates Apollo traces could last 10 to 100 million years.
The flags are another story. Ultraviolet light and heat cycles have probably wrecked the nylon long ago.

description:
What if Apollo's footprints stayed on the Moon for millions of years?
Without wind or rain, only micrometeorites erase them, and a lunar scientist estimates 10 to 100 million years.
What should we run through next?
